findings.title: Update re-POSTs secrets that already exist, so redeploying fails.
findings.body: On the update phase, `insertSecrets` sends every secret in `props.secrets` to `POST .../secrets`, which creates secrets. Secrets whose names are still in props are never deleted first, so a plain redeploy with the same secrets (or a changed value) sends a create for names that already exist. Cloudflare will likely reject it as a duplicate, and `insertSecrets` throws. The adopt path at line 239 has the same problem when the adopted store already holds those names. Fix: send only new names to the create endpoint, and update existing secrets with PATCH on `/secrets/{secret_id}`, using IDs from the list call.

findings.title: Worker binding uses the wrong type and binds a secret named after the binding.
findings.body: Cloudflare's Worker binding for Secrets Store is `secrets_store_secret`, and it binds one secret: `store_id` plus `secret_name`. This code sends `type: "secrets_store"` and `secret_name: bindingName`, so `SECRETS: store` either fails to upload or looks up a secret literally called `SECRETS`. At runtime the binding is a single secret with `get()` taking no arguments, not the `get(secretName)` store object that `Bound` declares in `bound.ts`. Fix: model the binding per secret (for example `store.secret("API_KEY")`), emit `secrets_store_secret` with the real secret name, and correct the `Bound` type and `WorkerBindingSecretsStore` to match.

findings.title: Changing `name` on update never renames or replaces the store.
findings.body: In the update phase the code reuses `this.output.id` and ignores `props.name`. It then returns `name: name` (the new name) while the Cloudflare store keeps its old name. State and the real store drift apart, and a later adopt-by-name will not find it. Fix: when `this.output.name !== name`, call `this.replace()` or rename the store through the API.

findings.title: Secrets Store bindings are silently dropped from wrangler.json.
findings.body: The comment says these bindings are handled through a `secrets_store_secrets` array, but nothing is pushed to any array. Any Worker bound to a SecretsStore gets a wrangler.json with no such binding, so local dev and type generation miss it. Fix: collect `{binding, store_id, secret_name}` entries and write them to `spec.secrets_store_secrets`.

findings.title: Unrelated change drops the describe-block prefix from test scope names.
findings.body: This change to the shared test harness is not part of the Secrets Store request. Scopes used to be named `describe/testName`; now they are named `testName` only. Tests with the same name in different describe blocks of one file now share a scope and state, so they can adopt or destroy each other's resources. Fix: revert this hunk.

findings.title: Bulk delete is sent secret names, but the API expects secret IDs.
findings.body: `listSecrets` returns only `secret.name`, and `deleteSecrets` sends that array as the body of `DELETE .../secrets`. As far as I know, Cloudflare's bulk delete takes secret IDs, so removed secrets are never deleted. The call either errors or does nothing, and removed secrets stay in the store. Fix: have `listSecrets` return `{id, name}` and send the IDs of the secrets to remove. `listSecrets` also reads only the first page of results, so a store with more secrets than one page holds will keep stale ones.

findings.title: Secrets are created with empty scopes, so Workers cannot read them.
findings.body: Each secret is created with `scopes: []`. A Secrets Store secret is only available to Workers when its scopes include `"workers"`. With empty scopes, the Worker binding this PR adds cannot read any secret it creates. Fix: use `scopes: ["workers"]`, or make scopes configurable.

findings.title: Assertion compares the ID to itself and always passes.
findings.body: `expect(secretsStore.id).toEqual(secretsStore.id)` runs after `secretsStore` has been reassigned, so it can never fail and does not check that the update kept the same store. Fix: save the first ID in a variable and compare the updated store's ID against it.
